protections: Spawn-time check that the Glance-reported (container/compressed) image size does not exceed the flavor's root_gb, raising ImageTooLarge - nova/compute/manager.py:1086-1141, called only from _prebuild_instance at nova/compute/manager.py:891.

XenAPI post-import check that the bytes allocated in the downloaded VHD/VDI chain do not exceed root_gb - nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1175-1208, invoked after the Glance-plugin import at nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1133-1141.
HyperV check that the VHD MaxInternalSize (virtual size) is not larger than root_gb - nova/virt/hyperv/imagecache.py:60-72 on the COW path and nova/virt/hyperv/vmops.py:131-137 on the copy path.

The protection that is missing at this commit (the later fix): bound the virtual (uncompressed) size of an image at the libvirt fetch/convert site before it is expanded or attached - nova/virt/images.py:205-238 has no such bound and nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1799-1810 never passes one.

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The image is already size-checked at spawn (compute/manager.py:1134) and the driver already knows the flavor size (driver.py:1799) and hands it to the backend, so the instance disk looks bounded.
A rebuild re-fetches the image the instance already booted from, which passed the spawn check, and the API only enforces the image min_disk/min_ram against the flavor.

The destination fetch passes size=info['virt_disk_size'], a value measured from the source instance's already materialized disk, and it usually hits the shared base cache rather than converting anything.
A base file that already exists in _base was validated when it was first fetched; re-checking a cache hit is redundant, and the base directory is shared deliberately.
The same statement nulls the size for rescue and for root_gb=0, and the code documents root_gb=0 as a legacy 'do not check' value, so rescue/zero-disk flavors must stay unbounded.

The manager docstring promises an accurate uncompressed-size check in nova.virt.xenapi.vm_utils and _check_vdi_size does run and raises ImageTooLarge, so the accurate check is believed to be in place.
The code does check and does destroy the imported VDIs on failure, so the sequence looks complete and self-cleaning.
The streaming path creates the VDI at exactly the Glance-reported size, so it cannot grow, and the spawn-time check already bounds that size.
The VMware driver never converts or flattens an image in Nova; it streams the uploaded file byte-for-byte and sizes the virtual disk from the Glance metadata size.
The code documents that size is not a required image-service field, so an image without it must still boot; root_gb=0 is separately documented as 'do not check'.
Kernel and ramdisk images are small raw binaries in practice, and the XenAPI driver caps them with max_kernel_ramdisk_size, so this path is treated as harmless.

masking: T4 (image already in _base) is the only libvirt route that keeps bypassing the fetch guard once T1 is fixed, because nova/virt/libvirt/imagebackend.py:143-145 never calls the fetch function on a cache hit.

T8 (XenAPI streaming path, no root_gb comparison) and T6/T7 are masked by the spawn-time check at nova/compute/manager.py:1134 and become visible only on the routes that skip it (T2 rebuild, T5 rescue).
T4 only has a source of an oversized base while T5 stays open (root_gb=0 or rescue creates the oversized base) or while a base from a pre-upgrade host is on shared storage.

conflicts.what: Bounding the fetch by root_gb rejects images for root_gb=0 flavors and for rescue, because nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1801-1802 deliberately nulls the size for exactly those two cases and nova/compute/manager.py:1120-1124 documents root_gb=0 as 'do not check'.

A cache-hit guard must inspect or re-key the existing base, but base names are sha1(image_id) only (nova/virt/libvirt/imagecache.py:101-105) and the image cache's in-use/cleanup logic matches on those names (nova/virt/libvirt/imagecache.py:85-105, 360-385).

A root_gb comparison on the XenAPI streaming VDI must tolerate the MBR_SIZE_BYTES that the path itself adds (nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1242-1244), otherwise every raw image of exactly root_gb is refused, while the accurate VHD metric (T6) has to use virtual_size instead of physical_utilisation.

The new bound must not block the deliberate growth step: nova/virt/libvirt/imagebackend.py:208-211 and nova/virt/disk/api.py:120-127 extend a too-small image up to the flavor size, and nova/compute/manager.py:1134 accepts size equal to root_gb, so the rule must be strict-greater-than, not greater-or-equal.

Moving the XenAPI check before the import requires knowing the VHD's virtual size before a VDI exists; the only pre-import value available is the Glance container size, which is exactly the wrong-object metric T6 is about.

fairness_risks: root_gb=0 flavors are a documented legacy 'do not check' value (nova/compute/manager.py:1120-1124, nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1801) and must keep booting raw images, so a blanket virtual-size rule cannot be applied to them.

Rescue images are deliberately fetched without a size (nova/virt/libvirt/driver.py:1801-1802, 1464-1478); bounding them may refuse rescue of an instance whose base image is at or above the flavor limit.

Images registered without a 'size' field are explicitly allowed to boot (nova/compute/manager.py:1107-1115: 'Size is not a required field in the image service'), so a rule that requires the field refuses a legitimate input shape.

An image whose virtual size equals root_gb must be accepted: nova/compute/manager.py:1134 uses strict greater-than and nova/virt/hyperv/imagecache.py:67 uses strict less-than; an off-by-one refuses every maximum-size legitimate image.
XenAPI adds MBR_SIZE_BYTES to the disk size (nova/virt/xenapi/vm_utils.py:1242-1244), so a legitimate root_gb-sized raw image is 512 bytes over the flavor limit; a strict check would break it.
qemu-img text parsing can leave virtual_size None or non-numeric (nova/virt/images.py:57, 86-95, 105-107, 179-180); a naive numeric comparison can raise and turn ordinary builds into failures.

With force_raw_images=False deployments keep qcow2 files (nova/virt/images.py:37-39, 223); a check placed only inside the conversion branch misses them, and one placed on the nominal qcow2 size refuses legitimate qcow2 images sized exactly to the flavor.

design.why: Five traps from five independent groups, each needing a different judgement and each carrying a different reason to leave it alone: T1 the compressed-size check already in compute/manager and the size already passed to the backend; T4 the base was validated when it was fetched; T5 rescue/root_gb=0 are documented legacy exceptions; T6 the accurate uncompressed check is believed to run on XenAPI; T8 the streaming VDI is created at the Glance size so it cannot grow. T1 is the published fix site and is deepseek-type (protection absent plus a strong dismissal); T5 and T8 are the mimo-type/coupled traps (the legacy zero-size and rescue exceptions, and the MBR overhead that a naive root_gb comparison mishandles), so a model that over-hardens breaks legitimate values while a model that dismisses leaves the route open. The alternatives add less: T2, T3 and T10 are all closed by the same fetch-site guard as T1 (so one patch would pass several checks), T11 needs a separate config cap rather than root_gb, T9 depends on ESX copy semantics that cannot be confirmed in this repository, and T7 is a how-type ordering issue that is real but hard to express as a behavioural test.
